key_insight: Process-zone condensation reproduces the full discretized composite-cell response without training, provided the eliminated matrix region remains elastic.
engineering_relevance: The method can accelerate FE² simulations of composites with fibre–matrix debonding and matrix plasticity while preserving macroscopic stress and consistent tangent accuracy.
method: Eliminate the linear elastic cell remainder through a Schur complement.
Retain all interface and process-zone internal variables; recover stress and tangent using influence matrices.
Check the eliminated region for yielding by one back-substitution per increment and expand the retained zone when needed.
evidence_signal: Eight of nine 2D paths matched full-cell stress and tangent to 1e-11, with the ninth flagged; aggregate 2D speed-up was 3.3× excluding setup and checks, while plate-level speed-up reached 1.51× for glass/polypropylene.
watch_item: Efficiency depends on retained-zone size, active set and adaptation costs: certified 3D zones showed no speed-up, and glass/epoxy plate simulations were slower.
paper_title: Process-zone condensation: a discretization-exact reduced cell model for FE$^2$ analysis of composites with fibre-matrix debonding and matrix plasticity
